answer: Resist sybils with a decaying work stake: each identity must keep a live ember of recently attested answers, refreshed each epoch or it goes cold and loses vote and grade rights. That ember grows only from unique, peer-verified work, so cloned keys do not stay warm. When two identities show a ripple of correlated timing or duplicate wording, both stakes are burned with their locked rewards. A yarrow sortition samples juries only from long-lived warm identities, so a burst of new keys cannot grade or admit itself. N votes cost N ongoing work streams plus the risk that one ripple wipes the farm.
